key_insight: The paper defines bounded-error quantum approximation classes and shows that, under standard complexity assumptions, quantum algorithms can certify better worst-case approximation guarantees than classical randomized algorithms for some optimization problems.
engineering_relevance: This gives a formal benchmark for judging whether a quantum optimization method is truly better than a heuristic by requiring provable approximation ratios and polynomial-time guarantees.
method: Define BQ-APX, BQ-PTAS, and BQ-FPTAS as quantum analogues of classical approximation classes.
Require a uniform quantum algorithm that outputs a feasible classical solution with at least 2/3 success probability and efficiently computable objective scores.
Use complexity-theoretic reductions to prove conditional separations and hierarchy results for specific number-theoretic optimization problems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports conditional proofs and example problems—Certified Maximum Order and Discrete-Logarithm Fitting—rather than experimental benchmarks or numerical datasets.
watch_item: These are worst-case complexity guarantees under explicit assumptions, so benchmark performance or heuristic success alone does not establish membership in the new quantum approximation classes.
paper_title: Quantum Approximation Complexity of Classical Optimization Problems
